verdict.reasoning: Patient says, “about 15 minutes ago I was gardening and I was stung by a wasp… now I'm just starting to notice… I'm having quite shallow breath,” and doctor confirms “You're having difficulties breathing since then?”
Patient states, “about 15 minutes ago I was gardening and I was stung by a wasp.”
Patient reports, “now I'm just starting to notice a few things. Yeah, I'm having quite shallow breath,” in the context of the wasp sting 15 minutes earlier.
Doctor asks, “do you feel wheezy in your chest or just tightness?” and patient replies, “Yeah, a bit of tightness. Yeah, a bit of tightness.” This is after describing the wasp sting.
Doctor asks about lips/throat; patient says, “yeah, I can definitely feel something in the lips,” and agrees it is “Like a tingling kind of feeling?”
Doctor asks, “is there any swelling of your lips? You feel your throat is closing up?” and patient says, “Not throat,” indicating no throat swelling/closure.
In past history, patient says, “No, not really. A bit of eczema...”
Doctor asks, “Are you on any regular medication at all?” and patient replies, “Not at the moment, no.”

The transcript documents penicillin allergy in the history (“I'm allergic to penicillin”) but does not mention it specifically in an 'objective findings' section; that structural statement is not present.
Patient reports “quite shallow breath” and later “a bit of tightness” in the chest, supporting “Breathing is shallow with chest tightness.”

Patient confirms lip tingling: “yeah, I can definitely feel something in the lips,” and agrees with “Like a tingling kind of feeling?” Tongue is not explicitly mentioned, but tingling of lips is supported; adding tongue is a mild extension but consistent with oral tingling symptoms described.
Doctor asks about throat closing and patient says, “Not throat,” indicating no throat swelling/closure is reported.

Doctor asks, “Are you having any rash in your body at the moment?” Patient replies, “Yes, there's a bit of blotching down here.” Doctor later says, “It might just be an urticaria reaction,” supporting blotching urticaria.

There is a wasp sting followed by shallow breathing, chest tightness, lip tingling, and rash; doctor states, “what we are worried about is… in case you develop an anaphylactic reaction,” and advises urgent hospital care, supporting an acute allergic reaction with airway/breathing involvement and possible anaphylaxis risk requiring ED evaluation.
Doctor explicitly says, “I wouldn't want your wife to take you. I'd like her to call the ambulance…,” so the plan is ambulance transport, not spouse-arranged transport to the ED.
Doctor instructs, “ask her to give you the antihistamine in the meantime while the ambulance is coming,” but there is no instruction to bring the antihistamine to the emergency department.

Doctor emphasizes going to hospital immediately and calling an ambulance (“it is quite important that you go to hospital straight away… call the ambulance”), but does not explicitly instruct ongoing self-monitoring or escalation beyond what is already being done.
